paper_title: VX-One: Typed, Calibrated Decision Heads for Real-Time Perimeter Triage - An empirical study of unknown-attack honesty, cascade gray zones, and calibration under drift

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Perimeter triage faces a latency/semantics trade-off: signature engines are fast and format-safe but blind to unseen attacks, while generative models are semantic but slow and produce unparseable output. In late 2026 a class of commercial System One decision models (TypeSafe Jev; Microsoft-Decision-1) began selling typed decision primitives - binary gates, closed-set choices, ordinal scores - as product APIs, with no academic treatment. We present VX-One: a small multi-head network (100K-10M parameters) whose outputs are these primitives - a calibrated gate, a choice over a closed candidate set that always includes an explicit unknown option, and an ordinal score, trained multi-task, temperature-calibrated per head (~0.7-1.7 ms p50 on CPU). We evaluate it on UNSW-NB15, CIC-IDS2017, EMBER2024 against calibrated XGBoost, Random-Forest, MLP, Kitsune, and measure a two-phase cascade (Suricata with 52,674 Emerging-Threats rules -> VX-One) over five days of CIC-IDS2017. Findings: (i) VX-One wins detection (AUROC/FPR@95%TPR) on UNSW-NB15 and under temporal drift on CIC-IDS2017 (0.711 vs 0.637), but XGBoost wins multi-class attribution on all three benchmarks; (ii) leave-one-family-out gate detects never-seen families on 9/9 UNSW folds yet drops below chance on CIC recon family, and abstention threshold transfers poorly across benchmarks; (iii) on payload-less reconstructions signature engines resolve ~0.1% of flows - gray zone ~99.9% of traffic, recovered by Phase 2 (combined recall >=0.978); (iv) calibration collapses under temporal drift (ECE 0.04->0.40) for every method while ranking partially survives. We provide a measured account of where typed calibrated decisions help perimeter triage, and where they fail.

sections.title: Start
sections.content: VX-One: Typed, Calibrated Decision Heads for Real-Time Perimeter Triage An empirical study of unknown-attack honesty, cascade gray zones, and calibration under drift Juan S. Santillana juan@jsantillana.com Independent research Abstract Perimeter triage faces latency/semantics trade-off: signature engines are fast and format-safe but blind to unseen attacks, while generative models are semantic but slow and produce unparseable output. In late 2026 class of commercial System One decision models (TypeSafe Jev; Microsoft-Decision-1) began selling typed decision primitivesbinary gates, closed-set choices, ordinal scoresas product APIs, with no academic treatment or independent evaluation. We present VX-One: small multi-head network (100K10M parameters) whose outputs are these primitivesa calibrated gate, choice over closed candidate set that always includes an explicit unknown option, and an ordinal score (conditional ordinal regression), trained multi-task, temperature-calibrated per head (0.71.7 ms single-event latency p50 on CPU). We evaluate it on three public benchmarks (UNSW-NB15, CIC-IDS2017, EMBER2024) against calibrated XGBoost, Random-Forest, MLP, and Kitsune baselines, and measure two-phase cascade (Suricata with 52,674 Emerging-Threats rules VX-One) over five days of CIC-IDS2017. Our findings are deliberately double-sided: (i) VX-One wins detection (AUROC/FPR@95%TPR) against every calibrated baseline on UNSW-NB15 and under temporal drift on CIC-IDS2017 (0.711 vs. 0.637), but calibrated XGBoost wins multi-class attribution on all three benchmarks; (ii) under leave-one-family-out the gate detects never-seen families on 9/9 UNSW folds yet drops below chance on CICs recon family, and an abstention threshold calibrated on one benchmark transfers poorly to another; (iii) on payload-less reconstructions of the CIC-IDS2017 days, signature engines resolve only 0.1% of daily flowsthe gray zone under payload opacity is 99.9% of the traffic, which Phase 2 recovers (combined recall 0.978); (iv) probability calibration collapses under temporal drift (ECE 0.040.40) for every method while ranking partially survives. We contribute not novel estimators but measured account of where typed calibrated decisions help perimeter triage, and where they fail. Keywords intrusion detection, calibrated decisions, out-of-distribution detection, malware classification, two-phase triage

sections.title:
1 Introduction
Operating a mitigation policy on the network boundary requires,
simultaneously: nanosecond-scale decisions on the line of fire, cal-
ibrated confidences that a controller can threshold, and honest
behavior on events that training has never seen. Three incumbent
technology classes each miss at least one requirement.
sections.content: (Snort (1) Deterministic engines [32], Suricata [28], Zeek/Bro [30], YARA [40]) are fast and format-safe but structurally blind to zero-day and low-and-slow offensives; the recurring failure mode is rule explosion that no operations team can maintain. (2) Text LLMs for security (e.g., SecureBERT [1]) bidirectional encoders, not autoregressive models, conflation we correctbring domain semantics, but as fine-grained decision engines on the line of fire they are heavy, and decoderstyle LLM agents add generation latency and output-format fragility that mitigation controller cannot tolerate. (3) Classical ML for intrusion detection performs well on tabular attributionXGBoost [5] wins our attribution benchmarksbut treats every event as membership test, producing confident misattributions on families the model never saw (Section 5.2). During October 2026, commercial class of models positioned exactly at this gap began to ship: System One decision models, sold as APIs that take structured state plus typed questions and return calibrated option probabilities (TypeSafes Jev [36, 37]; MicrosoftDecision-1 [23, 24]). No peer-reviewed academic literature covers the class, its evaluation is vendor-reported, and no security-domain assessment exists. This paper occupies the gap by building the primitives ourselves rather than remoting into vendor API. VX-One maps fixed-size event state to three typed decisions in single forward pass, then evaluates the whole pipelineincluding real signature engine in front of iton public data with anti-strawman baselines. The contributions are: typed decision engine (Section 3): shared encoder + three primitive headsgate (calibrated sigmoid), choice (softmax over declared closed set that always contains unknown), score (CORN conditional ordinal regression [34])with perhead temperature calibration on validation data, trained multi-task with homoscedastic weighting scheme [17]. Unknown-attack honesty, measured (Section 5.2): leave-one-attack-family-out across 9 UNSW-NB15 and 7 CIC-IDS2017 families, plus 4 months of EMBER2024 family drift, reporting both unseen-family detection (gate AUROC) and attribution honesty (how often the unknown option absorbs what the model should not claim to know). measured gray zone (Section 5.4): Suricata 7 with 52,674 live Emerging-Threats rules over flow-reconstructed CICIDS2017 traffic resolves only 0.1% of daily flows under payload opacity; the combined cascade recovers it with recall VX-One 26, October 2026, Juan S. Santillana 0.978, at the cost of measured precision drop on webattack days where Phase 1 is entirely blind. Negative results, measured (Sections 5.15.5): calibration collapses under drift for every method (ECE 0.040.40); class-weight tilts that help weak-label attribution can hurt it on saturated benchmarks; fixed abstention threshold is not portable across calibrations; dropping the unknown option raises macro-F1 by up to +11.2 pointsthe honesty/utility trade-off is real and quantifiable. Our heads are standard estimators; we say so. The claim is about their packaging and evaluation: event-level honesty instead of confident misattribution, measured end-to-end on data with audited labels [10, 20].

sections.title: 2 Related Work
sections.content: System One decision models. Microsofts announcement [23] and documentation [24] define the primitive triad (binary gate / closedset choice / ordinal score) with calibrated option probabilities and single-pass scoring; TypeSafes Jev [36, 37] commercialized the framing earlier in 2026. Both are vendor announcements without peer-reviewed evaluation; benchmarks cited (193.6 faster, 444.6 cheaper) are industry claims. Our work is the first academic instantiation and security-domain evaluation of the triad; we use their names only for attribution, define our own formal objects (Section 3), and deliberately avoid inheriting vendor terminology as if it were neutral vocabulary. Single-pass inference. Non-autoregressive originates in neural machine translation [13]: full output in one forward pass, no decoding loop. We use the term strictly for architecture (shared trunk, parallel typed heads). We do not claim novelty from singlepass-nessBERT-family classifiers are also single-passand our baselines include appropriate encoders; the differentiator is typed calibrated outputs, not one-pass-ness alone. Fast early-exit decision layers for per-event actions predate this design in spiritthe ViolaJones cascade [39] is their ancestor. Calibration and abstention. Platt scaling [31], multiclass probability transforms [42], empirical per-family calibration gaps [27], and temperature scaling [14] define our post-hoc protocol; conformal prediction [3, 41] is an optional wrapper we defer as guarantee, but audit empirically on the temporal split (Appendix A), noting that distribution-free coverage claims need exchangeability that temporal splits violate [4]. Chows reject option [6] and selective classification [11] ground our abstention semantics: with symmetric rejection cost the Bayes-optimal threshold is 1 𝜆𝑟 = 0.5, which is the threshold we initially set, and we measure how poorly it transfers where the model is overconfident (Section 5.2). Signature engines and their limits. Snort [32], Zeek [30], YARA [40], and Suricata [28] anchor the deterministic tier. The DARPA-critique tradition [21, 22] set the standard for dataset skepticism; audits of CICIDS2017 [10, 20] document systematic labeling errors. We use both stratified and temporal splits and audit against the corrected labels. ML on network traffic and malware. Kitsune [25] is the canonical packet-level unsupervised ensemble; we adapt it to flows (documented) and report its Platt-calibrated but weakly discriminative AUROC (0.61) as concrete instance of calibration creates no signal. Boosted trees [5] are the attribution baseline our engine loses to on all three benchmarkswe calibrate them with the same protocol to make the comparison non-strawman. EMBER2018 [2] and EMBER2024 [16], UNSW-NB15 [26], and CIC-IDS2017 [33] supply the data tiers. ViolaJones [39] is the ancestor of our secondphase-only-when-needed cascade.

sections.title:
3 VX-One Design
3.1 State object
Each telemetry event is compiled to a flat state
sections.content: (cid:1), 𝑆 = (cid:0)𝑥num R𝑑, 𝑥txt where 𝑑 {39 (UNSW), 77 (CIC-IDS2017), 2568 (EMBER2024)} and 𝑥txt are protocol-level categorical fields (proto, service, state) when the benchmark provides them (UNSW only). The feature stage 𝜙 (median imputation of non-finite values with row flag; signed log 1𝑝; robust scaling by train median/IQR; clip to 8) normalizes arbitrarily heavy-tailed benchmark features into fixed-size vector. Everything is byte-level reproducible from frozen JSON configs with single SEED=42.

LayerNorm → GELU → Dropout 0.1], residual from block 2) maps
𝜙 (𝑆) plus text-lookup embeddings to a shared representation ℎ =
𝑓𝜃 (𝑆), feeding four heads—one per typed primitive:

We deliberately use neutral head names rather than vendor naming conventions. Trunk depth/width by scale (𝐿, 𝑤): 2/224 (Nano), 3/576 (Small), 4/1280 (Base), with reduced input projections on EMBER2024 (whose 2568-dim feature projection dominates the parameter budget); verified parameter counts on UNSW-NB15 are 97K / 914K / 5.9M, inside hard 100K/1M/510M budget that is enforced by unit test. The choice heads open-set semantics are hybrid: where the training data offers real unknown population (EMBER2024s 2.19M-file unknown ground truth), the option is trained class; where it does not (UNSW, CIC), unknown is realized as abstention at decision time via (max𝑘 𝑝𝑘 < 𝜏abs), with 𝜏abs and any composed policy belonging to the mitigation controller, not the network.

sections.title:
3.3 Training formulation
Multi-task loss
sections.content: L = L𝑞, 𝑞 VX-One: Typed, Calibrated Decision Heads for Real-Time Perimeter Triage An empirical study of unknown-attack honesty, cascade gray zones, and calibration under drift VX-One 26, October 2026, with modified homoscedastic balancing [17]: per-task reference uncertainty with modified per-task reference uncertainty so that task-scale differences (ln 𝐾 vs. ln 2 for Choice vs. Gate) do not dominate the initialization. Per-class loss weights on Choice use sqrt-normalized, mean-1 tilts 𝜔𝑘 with an analytic de-tilt in inference (𝑧 𝑧 log 𝜔) applied before calibration, so the recovered posterior remains population-correct. The gate loss is unweighted BCE: weighting shifts the optimal logit by log(𝜔+/𝜔 ), an offset temperature calibration cannot undo. Training uses AdamW (weight decay 102 on 2D weight matrices only), linear warmup (5%) + cosine decay, gradient clipping at 1.0, mixed precision, and early stopping (patience 4) on validation loss. All backbone hyperparameters are frozen across datasets and scales (D11-like discipline).

sections.title:
3.4 Decision controller semantics
The controller composes three binary gates from calibrated head
outputs: the trained gate (𝑝cal ≥ 𝜏det, default 0.5); a drop gate on the
exact CORN marginal 𝐶2 = P(sev ≥ 2 | 𝑥); and a low-urgency gate
on the recon coordinate of the choice head. The severity rubric
makes both implications exact—sev ≥ 2 ⇒ attack and recon ⇒
sev=1—and they are verified with zero rule violations on 3.09M
labeled flows, so each gate’s target event coincides with exactly the
event its own head estimates.
sections.content: Gates are single-head functionals, by design. For single-head functionals, post-processing (de-tilt, temperature, thresholding) keeps the calibration error within bound determined by the heads own deficiency (Appendix A, Lemma 1). Across heads, no useful composition bound exists: two perfectly-calibrated heads can combine into joint policy whose calibration error is 1/4 in the worst case, whatever the marginal ECEs say (Appendix A, Prop. 4)and the 𝐴=𝐵 case that attains it (two heads estimating the same underlying question) is the realistic one in security. The controller therefore composes boolean decisions between gates and never probabilities between heads; any future composed gate must be rubric-reducible to single head, or measure its own joint calibration. Thresholds are cost statements, not constants. With uniform misclassification cost and escalation cost 𝜆𝑟 , the Bayes rule with rejection abstains iff max𝑘 𝑝𝑘 < 1 𝜆𝑟 [6, 7]: 𝜏abs = 0.5 is the statement 𝜆𝑟 = 0.5 (unknown costs as much as wrong attribution), and 𝜏det = 0.5 is the statement that missing an attack costs the same as false alarm. For operators who hold different cost ratios, the mapping is the standard cost-sensitive one, 𝜏 = 𝑐FP/(𝑐FP+𝑐FN) [9] e.g., 10:1 miss:alarm ratio implies 𝜏 0.091; we keep 0.5 as the declared default and expose the mapping rather than tune silently. General policies with full cost matrix live in the controllermaxprob abstraction can deviate from true Bayes when costs are asymmetric (an event with max𝑘 𝑝𝑘 above threshold may have lower expected cost elsewhere)and we measure the deviation of the abstraction on validation data rather than assume it away.

sections.title: 4 Experimental Setup
sections.content: Data. UNSW-NB15 [26]: 149,039 / 26,302 / 82,332 flows (official split); 9 attack families. CIC-IDS2017 [33] (MLCVE-corrected variant): 2.83M flows; two splits, stratified (sanity) and by-day (temporal drift). EMBER2024 [16]: 3.85M binaries; temporal split by week, with the public challenge set held out; 2.19M ground-truth-unknown training rows. Label errors in the original CICIDS2017 are documented [10, 20]; on top of the audited variant, we repair raw-label encoding artifacts (U+FFFD mojibake in the web-attack labels) and singular/plural naming drift (Backdoor), which naive ingestion would silently route to the unknown class; micro-classes (11 Heartbleed, 36 Infiltration flows) are retained rather than dropped and stratified exactly. Every count is checked against the frozen schema in code before any experiment runs. Baselines. XGBoost (500 boosted trees, hist mode), Random Forest (300 trees, min-leaf 1), an MLP (2256), and Kitsune (9-autoencoder ensemble with feature bagging, Platt-calibrated on validation)all trained with the same feature stage, the same per-class loss weights where analogues exist, and the same per-head temperature-scaling calibration as VX-One. This is anti-strawman discipline: boosted trees benefit from the calibration fix [27], and we report them raw and calibrated. zero-shot API baseline from the commercial System One class (Section 5.6) was planned; it was not executed this cycle. Metrics. Detection: AUROC and FPR@95%TPR (the FPR at the threshold capturing 95% of true attacksan operational line-of-fire number that accuracy-style metrics hide). Attribution: label-aware macro-F1 (GT-unknown rows excluded by label, as they have no known counterpart). Calibration: 15-bin ECE, MCE, Brier, NLL, and reliability diagrams, reported on raw and calibrated heads. Latency: single-thread, batch=1, 3,000 timed events, model-exact hardware recorded with each result. Infrastructure. Training on serverless GPUs (L4) with atomic checkpointing and tested resumption; evaluation computed locally from dumped raw logits so that all metric code is inspectable. 60 unit tests including end-to-end smoke training (pytest, 60/60 green).

5 Results
5.1 E1/E3 — Detection, attribution, calibration
Table 1 summarizes the two-tier comparison on test (calibrated

sections.content: (i) VX-One wins detection, not attribution. On UNSW-NB15 and temporal CIC, VX-One tops AUROC and FPR@95%TPR. On CIC by-day every methods achievable FPR@95 is degraded, but the trees degradation is total (FPR@95 = 1.0 no threshold reaches 95% TPR at nontrivial FPR), while VX-One retains partially usable operating point. Attribution (macro-F1) inverts this: calibrated XGBoost wins on UNSW, stratified CIC, and EMBER2024by 48 points. We report the inversion rather than hide it: our contribution does not rest on attribution wins, and we are explicit about the loss. 5.2 E2 — Unknown-attack honesty
Leave-one-family-out (LOAO): train without family 𝐹 , test against
𝐹 ’s held-out rows. Table 2 reports unseen-family detection (gate

UNSW: the gate generalizes. Nine of nine never-seen families are detected with gate AUROC 0.85, most above 0.95, while macroF1 on known families is preserved (0.380.56). The abstention rate on the excluded family ramps 392%feature-dependent, not tunedependent, which is exactly the honesty modulation we want (an unseen-but-gatelike family still realizes unknown 2892% of the time instead of being absorbed into normal). CIC: the failures are structural, not accidental. On stratified CIC-Small LOAO  (Table 3)  , the gate remains strong where families are textually distinctive (bruteforce 0.967, webattack 0.979, exploitation 0.970, dos_ddos 0.852), but drops below chance on recon (0.426) and near chance on infiltration (0.533, 𝑛 = 5): in 77 flow-statistics features, port scans from datacenter look exactly like benign port-touching client. Scope: what single-flow triage cannot see. This blindness is structural, and stating its boundary is part of the contribution: VX-One classifies isolated events (one flows statistics, one binarys features). Reconnaissance is by definition temporal-aggregation phenomenonlow-and-slow scans are invisible to per-event statistics and become detectable only in detection-by-behavior over time windows (event provenance, targets-per-time histograms, scanning divisibility). The perimeter architecture therefore does not rely on the per-event head for recon: Phase 1 (Suricata portscan signatures, which partially cover it) and any windowed detector sit in front of, or beside, the per-event gate (Section 5.4); when Phase 1 is payloadblind, the residual recon coverage is declared honestly rather than inflated. The abstention threshold measured at the default is nonportable: on UNSW, 𝜏abs = 0.5 abstains 392% on excluded families; on CIC, where calibration is saturated (Table 1, ECE 0.001), the same fixed threshold abstains on zero rowsevery excludedfamily event gets assigned to normal with high confidence. Undersaturated models are correctly selective, over-saturated ones are confidently wrong. Sweep: portable threshold does not exist (Figure 1). On UNSW the sweep admits operating points: 𝜏=0.5 abstains on 37.5% of excluded-family rows with 55.0% false attribution to known attack class, and rising to 𝜏=0.99 yields 97.3% abstention at 0.66% false attributiona monotone honesty/utility frontier an operator can pick from. On CIC there is no operating point: even at 𝜏=0.99 abstention reaches only 17.8% of excludedfamily rows; the dominant failure mode is benign absorption (94.5% of unseen-family events attributed to normal at saturated confidence), not scattering across attack classes (5.5%, the UNSW failure mode). Median max-probability on excluded rows is 0.999 on five of seven CIC folds (recon: 1.000), and the margin alternative (𝑝 (1) 𝑝 (2) , median 1.000 on recon) inherits the saturation: marginbased selective classification [11] fails for the same reason fixed thresholds dopost-hoc policies operate on the confidence distribution, and saturation has destroyed the information the policy needs. Rescuing confidently-wrong model requires recalibration on in-scope data (per-window, online), not sharper threshold; this is why abstention is mitigation with preconditions, not guarantee. EMBER2024 drift: trained-unknown as an honesty mechanism. The EMBER run trains on weeks 045 and validates/tests on later weeks; family composition drifts measurably at test time. Gate-robustness is high (AUROC 0.997, FPR@95 0.012). The family-conditional table is the interesting one: berbew, which grew 34.5K92K rows in test, retains recall 0.998; wacatac, which mutated, falls to recall 0.129 with 85%unknown; grandoreiro (𝑛 = 226, almost absent from train) falls to 0.221 with 78%unknown. The model does not reduce drift into false attribution; the unknown option absorbs what the model should not claim to know, and the gate keeps the operators safety threshold honest on the detection side simultaneously. This is the strongest single argument for the trained-unknown semantics (and contrasts directly with Table 3 on two ways of switching unknown on/off in Section 5.5). What unknown means under LOAO.. The two unknown mechanisms carry the same typed meaning but are not the same estimator. On EMBER2024, unknown is trained class with real ground truth (benign and tail malware), so its probability is an in-distribution rejection statement. Under LOAO on UNSW/CIC, the excluded family is not candidate: abstention runs on max-softmax confidence over the seen families, which is out-of-distribution similarity detection [15]the classic max-softmax baseline, with its known overconfidence failure modesnot calibrated probability about Scale Nano Small Base p50 (𝜇s) p95 (𝜇s) p99 (𝜇s) max (𝜇s) 675 955 1,652 715 999 1,795 773 1,022 2,082 853 1,059 2,335 the excluded family. We therefore report unseen-family detection (gate) and abstention separately and never describe the latter as probability of the unseen event. Both mechanisms lose informative honesty modes measurably (Tables 23); the design lesson is that distribution shift has no single calibrated fixthe honest object is the pair (gate, abstention), not one number.

sections.title:
5.3 E4 — Latency
Measurements use single-events, batch=1, single-thread CPU, 3,000
timed events per model, on each model’s exact released weights
(Table 4).
sections.content: Interpretation: VX-Ones typed decisions carry p50 inference cost of 1 ms on Small, making VX-One per-event inline decision component rather than sampled-batch tool. The commercial System One classs headline latency claims are API-level; level-by-level comparison is not apples-to-apples, and we treat them as context, not as competition.

sections.title: 5.4 E5 — Two-phase cascade: how much of the
sections.content: line of fire is actually gray zone We reconstruct five days of CIC-IDS2017 into PCAPs (documented reconstruction, no payload attacks HTTP bodies are not recovered, so content-only signature rules are expected to underperform and this is the lower bound they encounter on this traffic in the deployed position), run Suricata 7.0.10 with fresh Emerging-Threats Open rules (52,674 of them, concatenated) plus 8 of our own structural rules to level the playing field for header-only signals, then measure per family which attacks Phase 1 catches and what lands in the gray zone for Phase 2 to handle. Table 5 collates per day. The headline number is the gray zone under payload opacity, not universal estimate. Suricata with ET rules over flowreconstructed traffic detects only 0.1% of daily attacks by volume; the gray zone is 99.9% of each day in this reconstruction, and Phase 2 is what actually classifies it: the combined cascade retains recall 0.978 while precision stays 0.95 on every day except Thursday. We are explicit about what this experiment does and does not measure. It measures the Phase-2 recoverable share when Phase 1 is payload-blindthe operational regime operators of encrypted traffic (TLS everywhere, no payload inspection in managed switches) know welland not the real-world gray zone of deployment with full payload visibility, where Phase 1 resolves strictly more. Second, the cascaded numbers combine Phase 1 and Phase 2 events under documented independence assumption at the shared-flow level; signature-triggered attacks also perturb flow statistics, so true overlap is nonzero and our combined recall is an estimate anchored at the payload-blind lower bound (Section 6). The Thursday failure is the real lesson: on web-attack day of 456K benign and only VX-One 26, October 2026, Juan S. We additionally measured the adjudication quality of the composed policy as per-day riskcoverage curve (adjudicate attack iff Phase 1 flagged the flow or the Phase-2 gate exceeded 𝜏; abstain otherwise; risk = 1precision of the adjudicated set; Phase-1 leg exact per flow, Phase-2 leg exact per test row, composed leg under the documented independence assumption of Table 5). Findings: (i) the benign-only Monday is null point every adjudication is an error, so no operating point exists at risk 30%; (ii) on the Friday wave (DDoS+PortScan, 41% of flows) the composed policy admits 0.416 of flows at risk 5%, the whole plateau supplied by Phase 2 (Phase 1 adjudicates 0.0004 of flows at precision 0.067: under payload opacity it contributes latency and provenance, not adjudication coverage, Δ 1 point); (iii) the small-attack Thursday (0.5%) is where the cascade costs its own gate: Phase 1s 0.11% flag rate at precision 0.059 corrupts every composed operating point, so nothing is admissible at risk 10%, and Phase 2s clean core covers only 0.44% (min risk 0.3%). This closes the next step of Section 7.

5.5 E6 — Ablations
Table 6 summarizes the ablation suite (full 14-run table and per-
dataset effects in the released results). Four findings survive sanity
checks and are worth their ink:
sections.content: Text branch (a1). On UNSW the protocol/service/state lookups are worth 5 macro-F1 points and nontrivial AUROC. UNSWs original feature set is partly categorical field values (proto, service, state), so the text branch supplies exactly the vocabulary numeric encoder cannot infer. On EMBER2024 the ablation is an identity by construction: the 2,568 input features are already structural PE statistics (histograms, byte-entropy, imports), and no text field VX-One: Typed, Calibrated Decision Heads for Real-Time Perimeter Triage An empirical study of unknown-attack honesty, cascade gray zones, and calibration under drift VX-One 26, October 2026, Table 6: Ablations (ref = corresponding Small reference run). Calibration changes probability, never ranking (a3). Temperature scaling leaves argmax and AUROC untouched and improves ECE (e.g., 0.04960.0980 when removed, on the same logits). This is the expected signature of well-behaved calibration layer, and worth saying plainly because calibration is our semantic differentiator. Class tilts are not free (a4). On saturated CIC, removing the tilt 𝜔 improves attribution by +4.9 macro-F1the de-tilt pushes minority classes down in regime where the weighted cross-entropy had already pushed them up. On weakly-distributed EMBER the tilt matters less. There is no free class-tilt knob; its effect is deploymentregime-dependent, and our own loss design contains knob whose default is wrong for saturated datasets. We say so and flag the design revision. Dropout is dataset-dependent (a6). on CIC, zero dropout costs 14.7 macro-F1; on EMBER it gains +2.7 (the majority class dominates and early stopping regulates). No universal recipe; report per dataset. Unknown is measurable trade-off (a5-wide). Removing the trained-unknown option from EMBERs 11-way choice improves macro-F1 by +11.2 points (10-way is more balanced). Honesty is not free accuracy; making the unknown option available is deliberate spend.

sections.title: 5.6 E7 — The commercial System One baseline,
sections.content: measured We ran the zero-shot API comparison this cycle against commercial System One deployment that exposes the same primitive names publicly (single decision model, documented gate/choice/score questions; one API request per flow containing the three primitives over the identical frozen feature state we feed our heads). The sample is the protocol-fixed stratified draw (seed 42) of the UNSW test set: 1,000 benign and 1,021 attack flows, attack quota proportional to family with floor of 15. The vendor numbers are in Table 7; the gate is at chance on this distribution (AUROC 0.568, FPR@TPR95 Table 7: E7: commercial System One baseline, zero-shot, same frozen state and rows as our heads (2,021 stratified UNSW test rows). Vendor latency: 208 ms p50 / 591 ms p95; total run cost 2.2M input tokens (US$0.09 at the vendors published rate). An ablation adding an explicit unknown option to the vendors choice questionre-run over the full 2,021-row sample so the comparison is paired (identical rows; the only difference is the extra option) leaves the picture unchanged and slightly degrades it: gate AUROC 0.476 (from 0.568 without the option), macro-F1 0.066 (from 0.069), and the vendor assigns unknown to only 0.35% of rows (0.2% of attacks, 0.5% of benign). The escape hatch is available and unused: the gap is caused neither by the absence of an abstention option nor by prompt sensitivity, but domain adaptationthe generic triad zeroshot does not transfer to network-flow distributions. The papers positioning therefore still does not lean on beating commercial model; E7 closes the follow-up by measuring it, and is reported as an external stress test rather than contribution.

sections.title:
5.7 Discussion
Three threads bind the results together.
sections.content: (1) The honest triage division of labor. Where the benchmark is saturable (stratified CIC), trees win attribution and typed cascade adds nothing but latency reduction; where the deployment regime is adversarial (temporal drift, attack families that did not exist in training), the gate/unknown semantics earn their keep in detection robustness and attribution honesty even while losing the calibration war (E3). The contribution is the measured boundary of where typed decisions help, not uniform we win everywhere. (2) Honesty is distinct axis from accuracy. Section 5.2 and the EMBER drift table are the clearest pair of the paper: benchmark-optimal system (no unknown option, accurate operating threshold) maximizes macro-F1 while falsely attributing 85% of mutated family; the honesty-first system gives up 11 macro-F1 points on the choice metric and absorbs the mutation into an honest abstention. These are different products under drift, and the macroF1 column alone cannot distinguish them. (3) Saturation is deployment regime, not benchmark property. The same dataset (CIDS2017) produces saturated benchmark under stratified splitting and hard unsaturated one under by-day splitting, in both ranking and calibration. Any paper reporting F1 0.94 on IDS2017-stratified is measuring the models ability to fit monotone flow of re-used capture artifacts; papers should report the by-day numbers alongside (we do both). VX-One 26, October 2026,

sections.title: 6 Limitations
sections.content: Severity scores are rubric-derived, not human-labeled; the Score heads ground truth is documented familylevel mapping, so cross-level claims are approximations above benign/low/high/critical. Benchmark data, audited (Section 4): LOAO measures generalization across benchmark families, not robustness against real-world novel attacks; an honest reading of E2 is the gate generalizes more than the choice head, on these families not we detect zero-days. Single-seed runs outside the four main tables. The four main-table runs (UNSW Small, CIC strat-Small, CIC by-day, EMBER temporal) were re-run with seeds {42, 43, 44}: the seed-42 reruns reproduce the official numbers to the fourth decimal (reproducibility confirmed), ranking metrics move 0.02 points, and multi-class macro-F1 on CIC carries real spread (0.83 0.07 stratified; 0.34 0.09 by-daydrift instability, not implementation nondeterminism). The rest of the tables (per-family LOAO, ablations, E4 latency, E5 cascade) remain single-seed runs; conclusions that rest on differences >5 points are robust to this, but the small head-to-head diffs on CIC strat (cf. a2/a4 in Section 5.5) should be read as noiseborderline. Phase 1 is reference implementation (Suricata + ET Open + 8 structural rules), not our C++ engine; the claims of Section 5.4 are about the architecture, and the reconstruction means payload-content rules are at lower bound by construction. The combined cascade result is documented two-sample estimate under an independence assumption that is exact for full-family-invisibility cases and optimistic where Phase 1 fails on exactly the stealthiest subset; we state it as an estimate, and the per-day F1/gray-zone table it rests on is real measurement. Calibration under drift (ECE 0.40 on temporal CIC) is measured and now also audited by walk-forward perwindow recalibration experiment (E8, Appendix A): with one-day-delayed labels, gate recalibration (temperature or 2parameter Platt) recovers part of the loss (Brier 0.5390.504 on the hard day), but the oracle bound shows the ceiling is discrimination, not calibrationeven fitting the calibration on the days own labels leaves gate ECE at 0.445 with dayAUROC 0.56. Per-window recalibration is therefore cheap partial fix. Its prescribed alternative is also measured (E9, Appendix A): one to two passes of per-window continuetraining with delayed day-1 labels recover day-2 gate AUROC to 0.800.84 (four passes regress to 0.76) and, with the recovered ranking, the recalibration ceiling collapses from ECE 0.445 to 0.100.12but as-run day-2 ECE stays at 0.554 and no delayed-label fit recovers the new days composition prior, which lands on the abstention/coverage semantics of Section 5.2 rather than on any post-hoc map. Conformal wrappers are scoped, not promised, and now audited. Exact distribution-free coverage applies only under exchangeability: on the official UNSW split and stratified CIC, split-conformal coverage is exact [29, 35]; on every temporal split, family-composition drift is real and Juan S. Santillana measured, and coverage degrades at rate bounded by the calibrationtest total-variation gap [4]. domain classifier certifies that gap only from below (𝑑TV 1 2 BER; Appendix A)we therefore report empirical weekly coverage with exact binomial intervals and weighted variants [35], and make no distribution-free coverage promise; the measured EMBER audit is in Appendix (binary set-coverage within [0.895, 0.935] across all twelve test weeks; certified drift 𝑑TV 0.150.24). Cost-per-million is not yet measured from real billing data; latency, not cost, is the number we claim. Text-field attack surface (indirect prompt injection through user_agent, URIs) is real [12]; V0.1 has no sanitization layer and our text-branch vocabulary lookup (bounded 135-slot vocabularies, not free max-k) is only partial mitigation. Vendor-API baseline is single-point stress test (Section 5.6); we measured one commercial System One deployment zero-shot on one distribution (dense UNSW flows), not an exhaustive comparison across commercial decision models, prompt variants, or distributions. The honest reading is the generic triad zero-shot does not transfer to this domain without fine-tuning, not the vendor cannot be fine-tuned to this domain.

sections.title:
7 Conclusion
We built, trained, calibrated, and stress-tested a typed decision
engine for perimeter triage—the first published instantiation and
public-data evaluation of the System One primitive triad—and report
the boundary of its advantage rather than a uniform win: detection
robustness and attribution honesty under unknown families and
drift, a measurable gray zone of a live signature engine, and four
cleanly-measured negative results (calibration collapse under drift,
non-portable abstention thresholds, regime-dependent class tilts,
unknown-option accuracy cost). Six former next steps are already
measured: the vendor-API comparison (Section 5.6 — the commer-
cial primitive triad zero-shot sits at gate-chance on network flows,
and an explicit abstention option is not enough to close the domain
gap), the abstention-threshold sweep (Section 5.2, Figure 1—on sat-
urated deployments no abstention threshold recovers honesty, so
selective behavior must be bought with data and recalibration, not
with post-processing), the 3-seed re-runs of the four main tables
(seed-variance ≤0.02 points on ranking metrics; Section 6) and the
walk-forward per-window recalibration under drift (E8, Appen-
dix A—a cheap partial fix whose oracle bound shows the hard-day
ceiling is discrimination, not calibration), its prescribed alterna-
tive, per-window re-training (E9, Appendix A—one to two passes
with delayed day-1 labels recover day-2 gate AUROC 0.56→0.84
and re-enable oracle recalibration, while four passes regress and
as-run ECE is unmoved: weight freshness buys discrimination, not
calibration), and the risk–coverage curves of the cascade’s own
gating (Section 5.4—on payload-blind traffic the coverage at fixed
risk is supplied entirely by Phase 2, the benign-only day is a null
point where no operating point exists, and the small-attack day
is where Phase-1 false flags cost the gate itself). The remaining
next step is a payload-inclusive Phase-1 measurement to replace
